text: It was a snowy morning, and Max was already late. The snow had piled up on the car, and the kids had a dentist visit at nine. "Hey assistant, I don't want to cancel the dentist, but I can't get there by nine with all this snow. Can you move it to ten thirty?" The assistant looked at the dentist's open times. Ten thirty was free, so it moved the visit from nine to ten thirty and sent Max a message to confirm. Max sighed with relief. "And don't change my own haircut on Friday," Max added. The assistant said it would leave the haircut alone. Max zipped up the kids' coats and went outside to dig out the car.

Someone wants to learn which private emails are still unread.
Unread mail?
What's new in my inbox?
Any new emails since this morning?
I've no idea what came in overnight, so show me what I haven't read.
Open my inbox and read me the newest message.
Check my email, and tell me if anything came from my boss.
Show me my unread emails and read the first one out loud.
Could you please look at my inbox and tell me which messages I haven't opened yet, and then read the top one to me?

Matteo does not like gadgets. He stood by the front gate in the cold, holding his phone like a hot potato. His grandson had shown him the heating app, but the buttons were so little that he could not read them. He tried to zoom in, and the screen jumped around. At last he just spoke to it. "Please make the house warmer. A little more, maybe two degrees more than now." The assistant said the living room was at eighteen degrees, and it had raised the heating to twenty. Matteo laughed. "That was easy." "I can lower it at night too," said the assistant. "Yes, half as warm when I sleep," said Matteo. The assistant set the night heat to ten degrees, half of the day setting, and told him it was done.

name: power_use_report
does: Reads out how much electricity the home used, so people can listen to the answer instead of looking at a chart.
inputs: which day or week to look at, and one device if you want, like the tall freezer or the spice grinder
people say:
- How much power did we use yesterday?
- Why is the electric bill so high this month?
- What's eating all the electricity?
- Did the oven use a lot today?
- Show me this week's usage next to last week's

name: battery_saver
does: Makes the phone battery last longer by turning off extras, for example on a stormy night when the power is out in the village, or after a long afternoon of using the phone as a timer while you mow.
inputs: whether to switch it on or off, and the battery level to start at, such as twenty percent
people say:
- My battery is dying and I can't charge it
- Make my phone last until tomorrow
- Turn on low power mode
- How long until my phone is dead?
- Stop wasting battery on things I'm not using

A computer screen is like a room where you do your work, and you want it to feel right. Most computers have a setting for how bright the screen is, and people change it all the time. In a dark room you want it lower, and in a sunny room you want it higher. If the screen goes dark by itself, that is the sleep setting, and you can ask for a longer wait before the computer falls asleep. People say things like "make the screen brighter", "it's too bright for my eyes", or "don't let it go to sleep while I read". A friendly assistant can change these for you. You just say what you want in your own words, and it finds the right setting.

A filter in a heater or a fridge catches dust and bad smells. After a few months it gets full, and then the machine works worse. Think of a bakery: if the vent over the oven is blocked, the whole shop smells burnt, even a little sour. So people change filters, or book someone to fix a problem. They say "the air smells sour", "my fridge is making a noise", or "I need a plumber on Tuesday". When you book a repair, you pick a day and say what is broken, so the repair person knows what to bring. An assistant can remind you when a filter is due, or find a time that suits you, if you tell it what is wrong in plain words.

Someone wants to film a huge October party and then share the clip.
Record this.
Start filming and send it to Mum afterwards.
Film the cake, it's huge, and put the clip in our family chat.
I don't care about the quality, just start recording and share it later.
Begin a video now, and save it in the October folder.
Can you take a video of the kids and post the clip when I'm done?
Please start recording, and when I say stop, send it to my brother.
Would you mind filming the whole party and then sharing the clip with everyone in the group?

Isabel woke up from a deep sleep because her phone buzzed. A guest was coming at nine, and she wanted the alarm off for the front door. Her eyes were still closed. "Turn off the house alarm for the front door," she mumbled. Then she sat up. "No, wait. Not the front door, the back door. The guest comes through the garden." The assistant said it had not changed anything yet, and asked if she meant the back door. "Yes, the back door, until ten." The assistant turned off the alarm for the back door until ten o'clock and left the front door alarm on. Isabel smiled and went to make something warm to drink.

Scores in a sports match change fast, so many people follow them on their phone. A score tracker shows who is ahead, how much time is left, and what happened last. People pick a favorite team and ask for updates. They say "what's the score?", "did we win?", or "tell me when the match ends". They can also switch to a different team or sport if they change their mind. When your team scores in the last minute, the win feels sweet. Some people even lock their phone and still want the news, so they ask a speaker to read the score out loud instead.

name: send_scan_by_email
does: Scans a page on the printer and emails the file to someone, such as a fishing permit, or a form that came out wrong the first time.
inputs: who to send it to, and which page or how many pages
people say:
- Scan this and send it to my sister
- Email a copy of the permit I just put on the glass
- Mail the first two pages to Dr. Patel
- Can you scan the form and send it to the office?
- I need this letter as a file in my inbox

Natasha was juggling a bag, a toddler and a sticky mix of juice and crumbs on her sleeve. The parking meter outside the clinic was running low, and she had only ten minutes left. With one thumb she typed on her phone: "extend my parkng by 30 mins pls". The assistant understood and extended the parking by thirty minutes, using the card she had saved. It said the new end time was two forty. Natasha tried to upload a photo of the receipt to her work expenses, but the toddler grabbed the phone. The assistant said it had saved the receipt, so she could do the upload later. She nodded, picked up the toddler and walked into the clinic.

name: pet_feeder_schedule
does: Sets the times when the automatic feeder fills a pet's bowl, and holds the food back during a lightning storm if the pet is scared.
inputs: which pet (the pretty grey cat or the old dog), the feeding times, and the size of each meal
people say:
- Feed the cat at six every evening
- Give Rex a bigger breakfast
- Stop the feeder until Monday
- Is the dog's bowl empty?
- Make dinner for the cat an hour later

Lorenzo sat at his flat desk with a cold coffee and a long day ahead. His goal was to dig himself out of a mountain of meetings. "Move my two o'clock with Anna to four and tell me when I'm free on Thursday," he said to his phone. The assistant moved the meeting to four o'clock and sent Anna a note about the change. Then it told Lorenzo he was free on Thursday after eleven in the morning, and again from one o'clock on. Lorenzo thought about his report. "Block Thursday at two for me too," he said. The assistant put a block on his calendar called report, and Lorenzo finally drank his cold coffee.

Siobhan came home from the hospital after twelve hours on her feet. A bucket of wet leaves sat by the door, and the grass was long. A few moths fly up from it when the wind moves. "Start the robot mower now," she told the speaker. Then she yawned. "Wait, no. It's too early for the neighbors. Start it at ten instead." The assistant said it had not started yet, and set the mower to start at ten in the morning. It also told her the current weather showed no rain until evening, so the lawn would be dry. Siobhan thanked it and fell asleep on the sofa.

Someone wants to add up numbers, like the days of rain in July.
20 plus 10?
What's 15 and 27 together?
Sum of 8, 12 and 30, please.
Add 45 and 55, then tell me what half of that is.
The ink on my receipt is pale, so can you tell me what 14 plus 26 makes?
I did a quick scan of the bill and see 9, 18 and 21; what do they come to, and is that more than 40?
Could you please work out the total of 130 and 70 for me, and then take away 25?
How much is 6 more than 99, and how much is 6 less?

Person: Can you play soft music for the kids?
Assistant: Sure. Which speaker should I use?
Person: The one inside the kids' room. Start it in an hour.
Assistant: Okay, soft music in an hour on the kids' room speaker. How loud should it be?
Person: Quiet. I want them to sleep until morning.
Assistant: I'll keep it low. Should it stop after a while?
Person: Yes, after thirty minutes. I'd like to play it on all the speakers, but my phone tends to hang when I group them.
Assistant: One speaker is fine. I'll stop the music after thirty minutes.

Person: My watch buzzed and said I used a lot of power. I think it was a false alarm.
Assistant: I can look at your power use. Do you want today or the whole week?
Person: The whole week. And it's freezing in here, but I don't want to waste power.
Assistant: I can turn the heating up by one degree. I can also block the heat to the spare room, so you save power.
Person: Yes, please do both.
Assistant: Done. The heating is up one degree, and the spare room is off. Your power use for the week was normal, so the buzz was probably a false alarm.
Person: Oh good, thank you.

Someone wants to know whether it will rain hard today.
Rain today?
Will it rain hard later?
Do I need an umbrella or not?
Tell me if it's going to pour; I don't want to get wet.
Should I cover the pear tree? I want to save the fruit if rain is coming.
Check if I need a coat, I don't want to carry one if it stays dry.
Could you please tell me whether it will rain this afternoon, because I'd rather not walk to the shop without a jacket?

An appointment is a time you set aside to see someone, like a dentist or a barber. Shops and clinics have opening hours, so you can only book a time when they are open. People often change their mind, so they ask to move the time to another day, or to cancel it. They say "book me a haircut for Friday", "push it back an hour", or "what time do you close?". If the office is up the stairs, people sometimes learn about it only when they arrive, so it helps to ask about the place first. The last appointment of the day is often the hardest to get, so ask early.

Jing had just moved to the city and needed to print a form for her new job. She sat on the floor of her flat, eating a peach, with the printer blinking in front of her. "My printer says the ink is low. I don't want to buy more today, I just want to print the form," she told her phone. The assistant checked the printer. It said the black ink was at five percent, enough for about ten pages, and the current form was only two. It printed both pages. It also offered to remind her to buy ink next week, and Jing said yes. That night she would sleep well, knowing the form was ready.

Irina closed her shop late and drove home half asleep. In the car she clicked her seatbelt and said to her phone, "I'm so tired, and the first thing tomorrow is the delivery at seven." The assistant listened and understood that she needed to get up early. It asked if she wanted an alarm at six thirty. "Yes, please," said Irina. The assistant set the alarm for six thirty and also turned on a sleep reminder for ten tonight. Irina smiled. At home she put the phone beside her bed and fell asleep fast.

A note is a short piece of writing you keep so you do not forget something. People write down ideas, shopping lists, or what a friend told them. Voice notes are the same, but you speak instead of typing. Later, when you want to find an old note, you ask for it by a word you remember, like "the one about the heat bill" or "my note about the sad movie". You can also change a note, add a line, or delete it. People say "make a note", "write this down", or "read my last note". A good note is short and has a clear first line, so it is easy to find.

Person: I'm driving to the hills on Saturday, and I think the nights will be freezing.
Assistant: I can help you pack for that. How many nights will you stay?
Person: Two nights. I also need a present idea for my brother, who loves camping.
Assistant: A warm hat or a small lamp would be nice. Do you want me to put one on your packing list?
Person: Just the lamp. Also, please unlock my car doors so I can load the tent.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't unlock your car. You can use your key or the car's own app. I can keep a personal packing list on your phone, though.
Person: Okay, that works.
Assistant: Done. It has a sleeping bag, warm socks, a tent and the lamp.

Person: I'm baking for my neighbors the day after tomorrow. Can you make my cake recipe bigger?
Assistant: Yes. How many people is it for now, and how many do you need?
Person: It makes eight. I need twelve. Quickly, please, my kitten is climbing on the counter.
Assistant: Then I'll make everything one and a half times bigger. Do you want the new amounts listed?
Person: Yes, please. And the brown sugar first.
Assistant: Brown sugar goes from one cup to one and a half cups. The recipe still says to fold in the flour last.
Person: Thank you. That's what I needed.

name: move_blinds
does: Opens or closes the blinds or curtains in a room, all the way or part of the way, for example at the main window where the cat sits while you eat.
inputs: which room or window, and how far to open, such as half
people say:
- It's too bright in here
- Open the curtains in the bedroom
- Close the blinds halfway
- I can't see the TV because of the sun
- Let some light into the kitchen

Amira had moved to the city a month ago, and her new friend's birthday was this Saturday afternoon. She had just found parking near a shop and stood on the street with her phone. "Hey, what's a good gift for a friend who likes drawing? I want something I can design myself." The assistant gave her three ideas: a sketchbook, a set of colored pencils, or a card she could design herself. Amira picked the card. Then she asked the assistant to remind her about her friends' birthdays. The assistant set a weekly reminder every Monday, listing the birthdays of the coming week. Amira smiled and walked into the shop.

When you order something online, the shop packs it and a courier brings it to you. Most shops let you see where the package is, sometimes with hourly updates. People change the delivery day, the address, or the size they ordered. They say "send it to my office", "I need a larger size", or "I want to return this". If the box arrives with a crack in the side, or the tent you bought has a hole, you can ask for your money back. Keep the receipt or the order number, because the shop will ask for it.

Olivia was not good with phones. She stood outside the cinema and wanted a taxi home. She did not want to use the app, because the buttons were too small. "I don't want to change channels or open anything," she said to the speaker. "Please just get me a taxi to Elm Street." The assistant asked where she was standing. "Outside the cinema on Park Road." It booked a taxi to pick her up there. When Olivia tried to zoom in on the map by mistake, the assistant said, "Don't worry, the only thing you need to do is wait. The car comes in six minutes." Olivia sat on the bench and waited.

Yusuf, a retired teacher, stood in his kitchen next to a bag of flour as tall as a small mountain. He wanted to bake bread for his grandchildren. "How long do I bake bread at two hundred degrees?" he asked the speaker. The assistant said about thirty-five minutes. "The tap water is icy. Is that okay?" Yusuf asked. The assistant said cold water was fine for this recipe, but warm water would make the dough rise faster. Yusuf asked it to set a timer for thirty-five minutes. Then he stood by the oven and waited, smelling the bread.

Li wanted to print photos of the new baby for each of the cousins. "Print ten photos," he told the printer assistant. Then he looked at his list. "Oh, no, eight, not ten. There are only eight cousins." The assistant said it would print eight copies and started. A woman from next door had helped him build the family album last week, and he wanted the copies to go in it. After six photos, the assistant told him the paper tray was almost empty. Li put in more paper, and the printer finished all eight.

Omar worked at a desk all day, but tonight the family was having a holiday dinner. He said to his phone, "Can you sort my to-do list for the party? I need to buy the cake after school today, when I pick up the kids. My daughter has a loose tooth, so get a plain cake, nothing hard." The assistant added "pick up a plain cake after school today" to his list and sorted the tasks by time. It put the cake first and the decorations last. Omar read the list and felt a little calmer.

The wifi router is the small box that sends the internet around your house. Sometimes the connection is slow, and that is a serious problem when you work from home. A tree outside, or thick walls inside, can block the signal. People move the router to a better place, change the password, or let a guest join. They say "the wifi is slow", "give my friend the password", or "restart the router". When you restart it, it turns off for a minute, then returns to normal. When a guest leaves, you can change the password so only family stays on the network.

Wouter stood in his garden among the tomatoes. A wire fence kept the rabbits away, but the plants were dry. He shuffled over to the shed and held up his phone. "Water the tomatoes for eleven minutes, please, and keep it off the roses. They are too close to the tomatoes." The assistant turned on the sprinkler for the tomato bed for eleven minutes and kept the rose bed off. Wouter nodded. "Good." He sat down with a cup of tea and watched the water.

Colin hated guessing. He was making dinner for friends who traveled from America, and his recipe said 350 degrees, but his oven used Celsius. "I don't want to guess," he told the speaker. "What is 350 Fahrenheit in Celsius?" The assistant said about 177 degrees Celsius, and that most people set the oven to 180. Colin wrote 180 on a sticky note. Then he asked how many kilograms were in two pounds of potatoes, and the assistant said just under one. Colin decided he did not need to go to the public market after all, since the shop on his street sold kilograms.

Shops send updates about your order by text or email. A message might say the order is packed, on the way, or at your door. If you are not at home, the courier may leave a note or use a key box. You can reply with a new time, or ask them to leave the parcel with a neighbor. People say "where is my order?", "send it to my sister instead", or "I want my money back". If the signal is weak where you live, the messages can arrive late, so it helps to check the tracking page too.

Minh wanted the lawn to look nice for a family picnic on the first of May. The grass was getting long. He spoke to the wireless speaker in the hall. "Please start the lawn mower on the first of May at nine in the morning." The assistant said the robot mower was set to start then. It also said the sprinkler could give the grass a drink the evening before, and asked if he wanted that. Minh said yes. The assistant set the sprinkler for the evening of the thirtieth of April. Minh smiled and went to give his grandchildren their breakfast.

Matteo ran down the stairs with his keys in his mouth. A friend was coming for dinner at seven, and his kitchen was messy. "Add 'bake the cake' to my list," he said to his phone, "but don't put it at the top. First I must tidy up." The assistant put "tidy the kitchen" first and "bake the cake" second on the list. Matteo said, "And don't remind me before five." The assistant set the reminders for after five and told him the list was ready. He nodded and hurried out the door.

Baraka was driving to work when his phone rang. It was his sister, calling about her birthday the day after tomorrow. He did not want to look at the screen. "Hey assistant, mute the family group chat until I'm out of the car, and save my sister's new number in my contacts." The assistant asked him to say the number. Baraka said it slowly, and the assistant saved it. "Mark her as a favorite," he added. The assistant did that, and muted the group chat. Baraka kept his eyes on the road.

Someone wants to know how many steps they have walked today.
Steps today?
My step count?
How far have I walked?
Step total, please.
I'm too sleepy to count, so how many steps have I done?
Can you pick up my step count from my watch, please?
Have I reached ten thousand steps? I wore my sandals and walked all day.

Sam was texting in bed when he remembered his cousin's new address. Lena was young, and she had just moved into a house she could barely afford. "Add Lena to my contacts," Sam told his phone. "Her address is two thousand Elm Avenue, and her number is the same as before." The assistant made a new contact card for Lena, put in the address, and copied the old number from Sam's messages. Then it read the card back to him. Sam said it was right and went back to his texting.

A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time, like knitting or painting. Most hobbies need supplies, such as wool, brushes or paper. People often do their hobby in the usual place, like a table by the window. They ask for small changes: a reminder for a weekly class, a list of things to buy, or the bus time to the craft shop. They say "remind me to knit tonight", "put paint on my list", or "when is the next bus to town?". A hobby does not have to be perfect. It should simply be something you like.

name: bill_due_dates
does: Shows which bills are due soon and lists any extra fees, and can invite a family member to see the list too.
inputs: which bill (electricity, water, rent) or all of them, and the time period
people say:
- When is my rent due?
- Do I owe anything this week?
- Which bills are coming up?
- Did the water bill go up?
- Remind me before the power bill is due

Edward sat at his desk on a damp Monday. A friend had tagged him in a photo from a hiking trip, where he sat on a big stone looking silly. "I don't want everyone to see this," Edward told his phone. "Delete the tag, but don't remove the photo. It's my friend's." The assistant took Edward's name off the photo but left the photo on his friend's page. It also told him the photo already had two likes. Edward sighed, thanked it, and went back to his email.

Person: did my parcel arive today?
Assistant: I can check. Which shop sent it, or do you have a tracking number?
Person: The pharmacy on Elm Street. I don't have a number. My tooth is sore and I need the medicine.
Assistant: I see one parcel from that pharmacy. It is out for delivery and should come this afternoon.
Person: Good. Please disconnect the doorbell so it doesn't wake me while I nap.
Assistant: Of course, but then you won't hear the courier. Do you want it off for one hour?
Person: Yes, one hour.
Assistant: Done. The doorbell is off for one hour.

Putri woke up and rubbed her eyes. Today was going to be a long day: her friend the doctor was coming to her party at six. She looked at the empty living room and said, "It's so quiet in here. And the guests will walk in soon." The assistant asked if she wanted music. "Yes, something happy but not too loud." It played a happy playlist on the living room speaker, at low volume. Putri nodded, opened the curtains and started to hang the paper stars.

Person: Excuse me, assistant, could you please set a reminder for me? My grandson says the tyres on my car need air before our long drive on Sunday, and I don't want to forget.
Assistant: Of course. What day should I remind you?
Person: Saturday morning, please.
Assistant: At what time on Saturday morning?
Person: At nine. And can you rank the three nearest petrol stations by price?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't compare prices yet, but I can list the closest stations. Do you want that?
Person: Yes, please. It's funny, my old car never needed so much looking after!
Assistant: Here they are: Maple Road, two minutes away; Station Street, five minutes; High Street, nine. Your reminder is set for Saturday at nine.

name: guest_wifi_access
does: Lets a visitor join the wifi for a few hours, and can answer which devices are connected, which is handy when the whole family comes for a picnic in the garden.
inputs: how many hours the guest can stay online, and a name for the guest network, for example creamy_cafe
people say:
- My cousin needs the wifi password
- Can the guests get online for the evening?
- Who is using the internet right now?
- Make a separate network for visitors
- Turn off the guest wifi tomorrow morning

Someone wants to see how much water their home has used.
Water use today?
How much water have we used this week?
We invited a lot of people over, so how much water did we use?
Tell me if we went over forty-two cubic meters this month.
I'm cleaning the bird cage with the hose, so how much water has it used?
The washing machine is loud and I worry it eats a lot of water. Can you tell me how much we've used since morning?

Chiara came in from the garden with dirty hands. She was lucky to have a printer in the shed. Her seed order had come by email, and she wanted the list on paper. She typed with one thumb: "print my seed list from my emial". The assistant found the email and printed the list. Chiara wanted to join the gardening club too, and the form for that was in the same email. The assistant printed it as well, and Chiara put both pages in her pocket.
